question.text: A sponsor debates between PARALLEL and MASTER-FEEDER structures. Parallel is GENERALLY MORE EXPENSIVE than master-feeder because:

answer.text: Parallel requires SEBI pre-approval for every trade

In parallel, each fund (onshore AIF + offshore fund) has its own separate investment manager and charges a full management/performance fee, duplicating cost layers; in master-feeder, fees are largely centralised at the master level with only a nominal fee at the feeder
Parallel funds must pay higher SEBI registration fees
Parallel structures are not allowed to use custodians

explanation.text: The Logic: In parallel structure, each vehicle has its own manager and full fee layer — two managers, two fee stacks. In master-feeder, the master charges the full fee and the feeder charges only a nominal admin fee (USD 1,000 type), with management fee passed via NAV. Investors in parallel end up paying two layers of fees indirectly. The Trap: Options A, C, D are fabricated. Cost comes from duplicate fee layers. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/D both test this cost comparison. Manager's Pro-Tip: When pitching a new fund to offshore capital, offer master-feeder by default; parallel is justified only when specific investor-category segregation (different fee tiers, different investment exclusions) is needed.
